items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: George was a good drummer too... George Washington went with Buddy Petit.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. And Henry, Henry Zeno was playing the drum with, with Joe Oliver. Mm-hmm. Henry Zeno, he had a good little drummer too. Oh, fast. All him from his day. Mm-hmm.
What about George Washington, the drum with the player?

Oh, yeah. George was a good drummer too. He was a young fella. Yeah. It was George's dad. He didn't, get, get the beat famous, he passed away. Who did he play with? George was playing with, he split with Buddy Petit after, after Buddy Petit split his band up. And Morris, Morris Fletcher was playing with Buddy Petit. And after, he split up and Buddy, Morris Fletcher went with Kid Ren and George, George Washington went with Buddy Petit. Oh, yeah.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: They had George Washington, Eddie Morris. Now all the people was playing more trombone when I was playing.

ctx.x: Well, who was the best trombone player then, Norfolk?

A real thunk trombone player, you know what I mean? Well, I tell you, at the time then, you see Dick, tell you the truth, them was more of a musical man, but good man, you understand? And they could play jazz too, you understand? But there was more musical man, you know? India was always good trombone players. Now they had to take like, they had Boris Fletcher right around there playing trombone. They had George Washington, Eddie Morris. Now all the people was playing more trombone when I was playing. They were…
Did you ever see any vowel trombone players?
